statement: Define two sequences of indices A and B as follows. Initialize A = [0] and B = [1]. For i = 2, 3, ..., len(nums)-1 in increasing order, let a be the last element of A and b the last element of B. If nums[a] > nums[b], append i to A; otherwise append i to B. Let arr1 be the sequence [nums[i] for i in A] (in the order of A, which is increasing) and arr2 be [nums[i] for i in B]. The function returns a result r such that len(r) = len(nums) and r is the concatenation arr1 ++ arr2.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r and len(r) = len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), 1 <= r[j] <= 100.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r and r[0] = nums[0].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r and there exists an integer k with 1 <= k <= len(nums)-1 such that: (1) r[0..k-1] is a subsequence of nums, i.e., there exist indices 0 <= i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{k-1} < len(nums) with r[j] = nums[i_j] for 0 <= j < k; (2) r[k..len(nums)-1] is a subsequence of nums; (3) r[0] = nums[0]; (4) r[k] = nums[1]; (5) the multiset of values in r[0..k-1] together with the multiset of values in r[k..len(nums)-1] equals the multiset of values in nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r, and for every i with 2 <= i < len(nums), let p be the largest index with 0 <= p < i such that nums[p] appears before nums[1] in r, and let q be the largest index with 0 <= q < i such that nums[q] appears at or after nums[1] in r. Then nums[i] appears before nums[1] in r if and only if nums[p] > nums[q].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r, and the subsequence of r consisting of all elements that appear before nums[1] is a subsequence of nums, and the subsequence of r consisting of nums[1] and all elements after it is also a subsequence of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (i.e., it does not fail).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every value v, the number of occurrences of v in r equals the number of occurrences of v in nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: The function returns a result r and there exist two sequences A and B of indices (each in increasing order) such that A and B partition {0,1,...,len(nums)-1}, 0 is in A, 1 is in B, for every i with 2 <= i < len(nums), i is in A if and only if nums[max(A ∩ {0,...,i-1})] > nums[max(B ∩ {0,...,i-1})], and r = [nums[i] for i in A] ++ [nums[i] for i in B].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 3, len(nums) <= 50, all elements of nums are distinct, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.
